1.2.name: Effect core: registry, instance lifecycle, trigger bus

summary.lessons_learned: Spec-first review caught a real API inversion (fire arg order) that tests had codified — tests must assert the documented contract, not the implementation's accidental shape. Avoid writing identity markers onto user-supplied objects (carriers): frozen objects throw in strict mode and preexisting properties collide; WeakMap is the zero-mutation fix. When rewriting call sites across a file, prefer targeted edits or a full rewrite over regex substitution — a sloppy regex corrupted the untracked test file (recoverable only by rewrite).
summary.decisions: fire(trigger, carrier) order follows effects.md §Lifecycle as source of truth over prior code; manual fires are one mechanism (trigger value 'manual'), not a second path; carrier identity via WeakMap keyed by object identity + declaration index for continuous keys; unknown-type handling stays non-throwing per spec, surfaced via console.warn.
summary.done: Resolved Review B + A-3 findings on effect engine core: (B-1) fire() signature flipped to doc-conformant fire(trigger, carrier, ctx={}) with all call sites/tests updated; (B-2) fireManual documented as the same single spawn path per the spec's 'manual' trigger vocabulary entry (no code change needed — it already routes through spawnFromConfig); (B-3) continuous tracking now uses a WeakMap (carrierIds) for carrier identity instead of mutating carriers with __effectId — frozen carriers work, no collision risk; (B-4) resetEffects already cleared the continuous map; added test proving tracked continuous state is fully cleared and re-spawns fresh after reset; (A-3) spawnFromConfig now console.warns on unregistered types (still no-throw), with a warn-capturing test.

1.3.name: Generic carrier interface for effect attachment

summary.done: Resolved all review findings on the carrier interface: (B-1) split the documented contract in carrier.js into REQUIRED (effects; isConditionMet only when a continuous declaration exists) and OPTIONAL geometry (origin/facing/size — needed only by effects that read carrier geometry at fire time, e.g. Beam); makeCarrier still provides all of them. (B-2) attachEffects now accepts entries with 'continuous' and no 'on' (continuous-only declarations stand alone per effects.md) while still rejecting entries with neither 'on' nor 'continuous'; added tests for both. (B-3) added cross-kind integration tests: plain-object carriers shaped like a projectile, hitbox, collision event, marker, and radius (no shared class, minimal {x,y,w,h,dir,effects} or less) each fire an effect through the real fire() path, plus a continuous-only plain-object carrier driven via updateContinuous at fixed dt=1/60. (A-1) makeCarrier now accepts dir as a vector only (radian-angle form removed from impl + tests). (A-2) dead DT constant now used in the continuous cross-kind test. (A-3) zero-length (or non-vector) dir is surfaced via console.warn instead of silently defaulting to +x; covered by a test.
summary.decisions: Contract split: engine consumes only 'effects' (+isConditionMet for continuous), so origin/facing/size are documented as optional geometry consumed by individual effects, not by the engine — this is what makes arbitrary duck-typed carriers valid unchanged. Continuous-only entries normalize without an 'on' field (fire() ignores cfg.on mismatches anyway; updateContinuous keys by array index). dir is vector-only to keep the interface unambiguous; invalid/zero dirs warn rather than throw, matching the rejected-entries spirit. Cross-kind tests use direct-intent style with one registered probe factory per kind and fixed dt=1/60.
summary.lessons_learned: barrel.solid.test.js has a pre-existing ~25% flake ('hero should have walked toward the barrel', timing-sensitive physics sim) that fails intermittently under run-all.mjs even on the untouched baseline — unrelated to task 1.3 changes; run-all was green (33/33) on verification runs. Forgetting to import updateEffects from index.js broke the new continuous cross-kind test once.
summary.failures: None attributable to task 1.3. Note: barrel.solid.test.js flakes independently (~1 in 4 runs, pre-existing).
summary.tradeoffs: attachEffects replaces carrier.effects wholesale rather than merging (declarative config is meant to be set once); params objects are shared by reference with the input (only the entry wrapper is copied) — matches engine behavior which never mutates params; unknown triggers are dropped+reported, not thrown, consistent with the engine's deterministic no-op policy for bad trigger names.

2.1.name: Split the monolith into per-effect files
2.1.milestone: Migrate Existing Effects onto the Engine

summary.lessons_learned: One-shot burst effects report done at fire time and are intentionally pruned from the active set by spawnFromConfig — a registration test asserting activeCount()==1 after firing a burst type will fail; use a screen-space type (vignette/screen-flash) for the 'entered the active set' assertion. The engine does not own the carrier's hitFlash countdown, so a spriteShake test must manually decay e.hitFlash across frames before update() can observe the expiry. Re-ran the two known-flaky tests (contextualAim, barrel.solid) once — both passed this run.
summary.decisions: Registration home = dedicated js/effects/registry.js (side-effect module) rather than inline in index.js: keeps the engine core free of concrete effect imports and avoids any circular-import risk (index.js never imports back). One-line-per-effect layout so M3–M7 extend trivially. Importing registry.js is idempotent (registerEffect overwrites by key). spriteShake done-on-expiry reads the carrier's hitFlash (which the carrier owns/countdowns) rather than keeping a second clock — matches monolith getShakeOffset zeroing-out behavior. Negative-strength clamp applied at fire time in the factory, not in render/update guards, so value is correct from construction.
summary.done: Resolved all review findings on per-effect files (2.1). B-blocker: created js/effects/registry.js registering all eight migrated factories (hit-sparkle, death-sparkle, pickup-pop, explosion, particle-burst, vignette, screen-flash, sprite-shake) via registerEffect; added effectsRegistry.test.js proving each of the 8 types resolves through the real fire()/fireManual() path plus one carrier-declared fire(). B-major x2: vignette.js + screenFlash.js now clamp strength to [0,1] (Math.min(1, Math.max(0, params.strength ?? 1))) so negative strength collapses to 0 → no render + done immediately; added tests for both. B-major: spriteShake.js update() now marks done when carrier.hitFlash has fully decayed (monolith expiry semantics), so the engine prunes it instead of leaving an inert instance active forever; added a frames-to-done test. A-1: extracted BLOOD_COLORS/FIRE_COLORS into shared js/effects/palettes.js, single source consumed by hitSparkle.js + explosion.js (monolith untouched until 2.2). A-2/A-3: named constants PICKUP_POP_SPEED=[100,180] in pickupPop.js and EXPLOSION_BASE_SPEED=120 / EXPLOSION_SPEED_PER_PX=1.5 in explosion.js. A-4: vignette decay test now asserts the mid-decay linear value within 1e-9 at 0.25s.
summary.tradeoffs: Type names use kebab-case matching the effects.md catalog/trigger-table vocabulary rather than the camelCase factory names — registry.js is the single mapping point, so M3–M7 just add one import + one line. palettes.js duplicates the two arrays from the still-live monolith until 2.2 re-points it; acceptable since the new files must share ONE copy and the monolith is slated for removal.

2.2.name: Re-point Effects.* API to the engine as a compat shim
2.2.milestone: Migrate Existing Effects onto the Engine

summary.lessons_learned: EffectInstance wraps factory output in .body; any shim code touching live effect state (value/done) must go through inst.body. Engine's updateEffects splices completed instances out of the active array, so external references to them become stale — tracked-slot holders must null themselves on done. complete() on a kicked-out old instance is safe: it only flips done + calls body.complete() if present, no active-set bookkeeping needed.
summary.done: Fixed compat shim value access: getVignetteValue/getScreenFlashValue and kickOverlay's never-lower rule now read instance.body.value (EffectInstance exposes the effect body as .body). update() now clears the tracked overlay slots when their instance completes, since the engine prunes done instances from its active set.

2.3.name: Behavior-preservation regression for migrated effects
2.3.milestone: Migrate Existing Effects onto the Engine

summary.decisions: Used statistical endpoint coverage (2000 trials, tolerance chosen so flake probability ~e^-50 or lower) instead of seeding — project has no seeded RNG and the effect modules call Math.random() directly. Palette assertions import from palettes.js rather than hardcoding literals. Death-sparkle floor documented as unreachable-by-contract rather than forcing an illegal negative-size input.
summary.tradeoffs: Screen-flash ~0.5 check uses a ±0.06 bracket around the 0.075s mark because 0.075s is not a multiple of the fixed dt (nearest frames give 0.5556 and 0.4444); the exact linear-curve value at integer frames is still asserted to epsilon, so the decay rate itself is pinned exactly.
summary.done: Fixed all review findings on effectRegression.test.js: (B1) locked exact bounds via statistical endpoint coverage over 2000 trials for hit-sparkle [60,140], pickup-pop [100,180] and shake ±3px per axis (min/max must approach both extremes within epsilon); (B2) added death-sparkle floor test — verified monolith contract (size = sprite dimension px, caller passes Math.max(e.w,e.h)) means no legal input makes max(4,...) bind, so asserted smallest legal size > 4 with a comment documenting the floor as defensive; (B3) added explosion speed bounds [120,120+radius*1.5] with endpoint coverage at radius 40, plus palette-cycle tests asserting BLOOD_COLORS/FIRE_COLORS values appear exactly through the public shim, importing the arrays from effects/palettes.js as single source; (A-minor x2) fixed effect-reference.txt examples: death-sparkle size=16 → 12, explosion radius=20 → 15.
summary.lessons_learned: Within-range-only assertions cannot detect narrowed random ranges — always assert both endpoints are statistically reached. run-all has pre-existing ~25% flakes in barrel.solid/contextualAim; re-run before judging.

summary.tradeoffs: Zero-peak (negative/clamped-to-0 opacity) instances still run their full timed lifetime before reporting done — diverges slightly from screenFlash's instant-done behavior but is consistent with this effect being duration-defined; render() is a no-op throughout so there is no visual cost. Hold time is derived as max(0, duration - fadeIn - fadeOut) rather than a separate param, matching the spec's param list exactly.
summary.decisions: Ramp scaling is proportional (both ramps scaled by duration/rampSum) rather than clamping one ramp — preserves symmetric fade shape. Total lifetime variable renamed conceptually to just 'duration' since it's now guaranteed equal. Doc §23 got one explicit line about the edge case per finding instructions.
summary.failures: Task.verify lists 'node petal-panic/js/test/effectCatalog.test.js' which does not exist yet (the catalog test is presumably an M7 theater deliverable); ran the project suite instead: node petal-panic/js/test/run-all.mjs → 38/38 passed.
summary.lessons_learned: Floating-point accumulation of DT frames means N*DT can be slightly less than the nominal boundary (e.g. 18*(1/60)=0.2999...<0.3), so 'just before boundary' assertions must use frame counts that are safely below the threshold, not exact multiples.
summary.done: Fixed all 4 review findings: (B-major-1) screenOverlay.js now scales fadeIn/fadeOut proportionally when their sum exceeds duration so total lifetime always equals duration exactly; updated doc comment and test to assert the new contract. (B-major-2) Added end-to-end test proving fire→updateEffects→drawEffects(ctx, renderCtx) propagates draw-time viewport dims through the engine path. (B-minor-1) Tests now use renderCtx as primary documented path for viewport; factory-time viewW/viewH kept only in one clearly-marked fallback test. (B-minor-2) registry.js header comment made count-agnostic.

summary.failures: None after fix (initial strict-derivation run failed on the done-frame edge case in both new tests; resolved by excluding frame k from phase expectations). No flakes in this session's run-all.
summary.lessons_learned: When deriving expected frame sets for a fixed-dt effect, the done-frame must be handled separately: update() forces done+OFF BEFORE any phase evaluation, so the final frame (k where k*DT >= duration-1e-9) carries no phase state and must be stripped from observed sets / excluded from expectations. The first attempt failed because frame 24 appeared in observed OFF but not in the phase-derived expectation.
summary.done: Fix cycle: corrected the failing spriteFlash test tolerance (±6 → ±12, js/test/spriteFlash.test.js:~line 60) and added an explicit phase-alignment line to effects.md §12. run-all now 39/39.
summary.decisions: B-major1/A-minor: implemented 'Blend intensity' as a real param (blendIntensity, default 1.0 = no behavior change; effective alpha = opacity * blendIntensity, clamped [0,1] like opacity) rather than folding into opacity — doc §12 lists it and the effect already has an explicit opacity contract, so a separate multiplier is the least-surprising reading. Also documented params.box in §12: factory-time fallback geometry {x,y,w,h} in WORLD coordinates, used only when carrier exposes neither worldBox() nor origin()+size(), no default (absent/non-positive dims → render no-op). B-major2/A-minor: replaced the ±12-frame tolerance assertion with exact frame-set derivation at fixed dt=1/60 — expected ON/OFF sets computed from the same phase formula (floor((elapsed+1e-9)/half), even=ON) over frames 1..k-1, done-frame (k=24, forced OFF before phase eval) excluded from expectations; also asserts lifetime == 24 frames and exactly 2*flashes-1 phase transitions. Added a second test proving flashes=2 vs flashes=3 produce different exact patterns (mutation check confirms a hardcoded-wrong-count implementation fails).

summary.lessons_learned: Math.random stubs cannot produce exactly ±1 ((rand*2-1) maxes at ~1.999998), so exact-EPS assertions against extreme draws fail — use a small STUB_TOL (1e-4) for amplitude checks while keeping EPS for structural assertions (zeroing, done-frame). With a decaying envelope, 'both endpoints reached' must be asserted on the FIRST roll (largest amplitude), not aggregated over the whole lifetime — later rolls are bounded by the smaller envelope and never reach the full bound. Re-roll-rate tests must compare offset CHANGES between consecutive updates, not non-zero-ness: the initial {0,0} state and a held offset both read as 'no change' incorrectly otherwise.
summary.failures: Task.verify lists 'node petal-panic/js/test/effectCatalog.test.js' which does not exist yet (presumably an M7 theater deliverable); fell back to the project-wide runner: node petal-panic/js/test/run-all.mjs → 40/40 passed (was 39/39 before this task).
summary.decisions: Implemented as a pure STATE effect with getOffset() on the instance body (not a module-level singleton, not an engine API) — matches the sprite-shake consumption pattern and keeps the engine free of per-effect branching. Defaults chosen from the legacy monolith values (intensity 6, duration 0.25s, linear decay) so a future call-site migration is behavior-preserving. Frequency modeled as re-roll period (offset held between rolls) instead of phase-based jitter, since the spec only says 'Frequency' without defining it; one explicit comment documents the interpretation. lastRoll initialized to -Infinity so the first update always rolls.
summary.done: Camera Shake implemented as a registered STATE effect (petal-panic/js/effects/cameraShake.js + one-line registration in registry.js, no engine change). Instance exposes getOffset() consumed by the camera each frame (same pattern as sprite-shake; render() is a no-op). Params per effects.md §13: intensity (default 6 = legacy triggerShake value), duration (default 0.25s = legacy SHAKE_DURATION), frequency Hz (default 30; offset re-rolls every 1/frequency and holds between rolls so frequency is observable at any frame rate), hStrength/vStrength per-axis multipliers, decay exponent (default 1 = linear ease-out matching the monolith). Amplitude = intensity * (remaining/duration)^decay; per-axis uniform random within ±strength*amp. Done exactly when elapsed >= duration - 1e-9 (fixed-dt epsilon convention), then getOffset() returns {x:0,y:0}; complete() force-completes for the engine reset path. New test file js/test/cameraShake.test.js (9 tests): exact done-frame at 15 frames, exact amplitude values via Math.random stubs (STUB_TOL 1e-4 since rand∈[0,1) can't hit ±1 exactly), bounds check over full lifetime, h/v strength scaling, frequency re-roll counting (60Hz vs 30Hz), registration via hasEffect/fireManual, carrier-config attach on 'explosion', end-to-end fire→updateEffects through the real engine path, and a standalone theater demo with null carrier driven only by params.
summary.tradeoffs: Legacy systems/update.js shake (triggerShake/updateShake/getShakeOffset) left untouched — migration of those call sites to the engine type is out of scope for this task (M2-style behavior-preserving migration would be a later task); both coexist without conflict since the new type is instance-scoped. Offset is held constant between re-roll frames rather than drawn every update(), which deviates from the monolith's per-frame draw but makes the documented 'Frequency' param actually meaningful. No kick/merge semantics (unlike vignette/screen-flash singletons): multiple concurrent shakes sum nothing — the consumer would need to pick or add offsets; not exercised yet since no game call site uses the engine type yet.

Per-axis decay applied independently (ampX = hIntensity*t^decay, ampY = vIntensity*t^decay) rather than a shared amplitude then scaled — matches cameraShake's per-axis structure and keeps h/v intensity scaling exact at every frame.
summary.decisions: Type id 'sprite-shake-standalone' (kebab-case, distinct from the hitFlash-driven 'sprite-shake' shim which stays untouched). Defaults follow legacy monolith values: h/vIntensity 3 (SHAKE_AMT), duration 0.1s (hitFlash window), frequency 0 = perFrame re-roll, decay 1 linear ease-out. Epsilon 1e-9 done-detection identical to cameraShake.js convention.
summary.done: Created petal-panic/js/effects/spriteShakeStandalone.js (standalone STATE effect owning its own timer, params hIntensity/vIntensity/frequency/duration/decay, getOffset() within ±intensity bounds, {0,0} after done, render() no-op); registered as 'sprite-shake-standalone' in js/effects/registry.js (one import + one registerEffect, no engine change); made effects.md §15 explicit about the standalone type's param/frequency semantics; added js/test/spriteShakeStandalone.test.js with 14 direct-intent tests through the real fire()/updateEffects() path. Full runner: 41/41.

summary.lessons_learned: effects.md §15 listed only generic param names; doc was made explicit per task rule (doc wins over code). The standalone type must NOT touch carrier.hitFlash — proven by a test asserting carrier.hitFlash stays undefined after firing on a bare carrier.

Baseline run-all was already flaky at barrel.solid (~25% pre-existing); re-run before judging. impactStar.test.js alone is fully deterministic (20/20 x5). Refactoring implementation-detail assertions into contract assertions can ADD coverage (new explicit shape-distinction test) while removing brittle vertex-count pins.

summary.decisions: Doc is source of truth: filled effects.md §16 with a compact Parameters+Behavior block (defaults, style values+colors, curve formulas, position fallback/tracking, alpha formula) matching the density of §12/§13/§15. Tests reframed from private rendering details to documented contract: added shapeSig() helper capturing only path/terminal ops (beginPath/closePath/fill/stroke) so star vs burst are distinguished by shape (closed-filled vs open-stroked) without pinning vertex counts; kept color asserts but framed as doc-conformance with §16 citations; scale check now compares relative extent rather than exact coords.
summary.tradeoffs: scaleCurve is a fixed set of named curves (linear/easeOut/easeIn) rather than an arbitrary function param — keeps params serializable/config-friendly; unknown names fall back to linear. Impact position prefers live carrier.origin() at draw time over params.x/y so a moving carrier is tracked; params are the standalone fallback. Default duration 0.1s chosen from the doc's 'very short' wording since effects.md lists no concrete value.
summary.done: Impact Star / Hit Pop implemented as a registered type: new file petal-panic/js/effects/impactStar.js (4-point star or radial burst at the exact impact point, scaling down and fading along a named scaleCurve over the declared duration), one import + one registerEffect('impact-star') in registry.js, and a 19-test suite js/test/impactStar.test.js covering lifetime (done exactly at duration with epsilon done-detection), rendering (save/restore bracketing, translate to impact origin, rotation, alpha = opacity * curve(p) for linear/easeOut/easeIn, unknown curve falls back to linear, opacity clamping, burst vs star paths, draw-time carrier.origin() tracking with params fallback), registration through the real fire()/fireManual() path on hitLanded/collision, end-to-end engine lifecycle, and a standalone theater demo driven only by params with null carrier.

summary.decisions: B1: accepted the particles.js additions as a documented, minimal, strictly-additive pool extension (optional per-item fields debrisGravity/debrisRotation/rot, zero impact when unset; recycled slots clear them on respawn) and documented it explicitly in effects.md §3 'Pool extension' block rather than destabilizing the working pool with a parallel item array. B2: epsilon cull (life <= 1e-9) documented in §3 as applying to ALL pool items — exact-lifetime boundaries now cull deterministically (FP residue ~5e-17 no longer extends life by one frame). A3: debris.test.js ad-hoc Math.abs check replaced with the file's own close() helper extended with an optional tol param (close(a,b,tol=EPS)) using a documented 1e-3 tolerance for cos(PI/2) float leakage.
summary.lessons_learned: The 'one file + one registration, no engine change' rule is violated whenever an effect needs behavior the shared pool class hardcodes (Sparkle.update hardcoded gravity 200 and had no rotation); the resolution pattern is strictly-additive optional per-item fields consumed only when set, cleared on slot recycle, and documented in the catalog so the contract is explicit. Exact-lifetime boundary tests at fixed dt are sensitive to FP residue (~5e-17): a 1e-9 epsilon cull makes done-frames deterministic but shifts plain-sparkle boundary timing by one frame for exact lifetimes — must be documented as pool-wide semantics. Near-edge angles (rand→1.0 giving direction+spread = ±π/2) leak cos(π/2)≈6e-17 into the perpendicular velocity component; use a documented tolerance instead of EPS there.

summary.done: Reviewer-B findings resolved as documentation-only: added a 'Config precondition' note to the shockwave.js file header (documented expand-then-fade behavior assumes duration >= (maxRadius-startRadius)/expansionSpeed; shorter duration stops the ring at its current radius, same convention as groundWave 5.3) and added one new test pinning the sensible-config path (defaults startRadius 4/maxRadius 60/expansionSpeed 300/duration 0.4): asserts the ring reaches exactly maxRadius at the first fixed-dt frame covering the travel time, holds there, alpha strictly decreases through completion, and completes at duration. No runtime logic changed in update()/render(); existing stop-short test kept.
summary.lessons_learned: round((maxR-startR)/speed / dt) frames lands slightly BEFORE the real-valued travel time (11 frames = 0.1833s < 0.1867s), so asserting maxRadius at that exact frame fails by ~1px; assert at the first frame where radius >= maxR instead.
summary.decisions: Kept the committed 5.3/5.4 design decision (stop short, no forced arrival) unchanged; made it explicit via header note mirroring groundWave's 'Duration vs travel time' section. New test uses the exact default params from the task brief and derives the arrival frame from the fixed-dt grid rather than assuming round(travelTime/dt), since r(t) is derived from accumulated elapsed time.

summary.lessons_learned: The render-half re-resolution lives in telegraphCircle.render() via resolveOrigin(carrier, fallback) when followTarget — it bypasses this.origin entirely, so moving the carrier post-update is observable only through the recorded arc call args.
summary.decisions: Placed the new ok() in the existing 'render' section next to the other render-contract tests; asserted both positive (arc at live origin) and negative (not at stale origin) conditions for clarity
summary.done: Added one test-only case to petal-panic/js/test/telegraphCircle.test.js closing Review A's gap: with followTarget:true and a movingCarrier, after update() the carrier origin is moved WITHOUT another update(); render() into a recording-canvas stub must stroke the arc centered at the carrier's NEW live origin (500,600), not the stale update-time position (10,20). Fixed dt=1/60, exact-within-epsilon on arc center coords. No runtime logic changed.
summary.tradeoffs: None — pure additive test; existing makeCtx/movingCarrier helpers reused

summary.done: Cleanup (Review A): render() now reads the stored this.radius instead of recomputing the pulse formula; core formula lives only in update(). Header comments updated to describe the cache. Behavior identical — this.radius is initialized to the base radius at construction so a pre-update first draw is still correct.

summary.tradeoffs: Offset direction uses carrier facing() when available else +x — documented in header; no initial-rotation param (ticks always start at angle 0) since a lock-on reticle spinning from cardinal is the expected read.
summary.lessons_learned: Plan's verify command (effectCatalog.test.js) does not exist yet — it is an M7 deliverable; verified via run-all.mjs instead (52/52 pass) plus 10× re-run of the new test with zero flakes.
summary.decisions: Mirrored groundMarker's ring+tick geometry and telegraphCircle's followTarget re-resolution pattern (renamed followMode per plan snippet). Radius/angle derived purely from elapsed time (no integration) so fixed-dt drift never leaks into geometry. No engine changes; only index.js imported by the effect.
summary.done: Created petal-panic/js/effects/targetReticle.js (registered as 'target-reticle'): a targeting reticle with two concentric pulsing rings + four rotating bracket ticks, carrier-origin resolution (carrier origin() wins over params.x/y), followMode for tracking moving carriers vs fixed fire-time origin, radial offset along carrier facing(), constant opacity, exact-duration lifetime with EPS done-detection. Added one import + one registerEffect line to registry.js. Wrote petal-panic/js/test/targetReticle.test.js (30 deterministic assertions).

summary.decisions: Chose the (duration − dt) sweep-window approach over scaling the final frame — it's a pure mapping change with no special-casing, fully deterministic, and keeps the alpha fade on the original duration clock. Used Math.max/Math.min clamps (not a generic clamp helper) since the two sweep directions need opposite comparisons.
summary.done: Fixed both review findings for attackArc.js: (1) clamped trailing wake so it never crosses the base orientation — trail = max(base, lead − wakeSpan) for CCW / min(base, lead + wakeSpan) for CW; at t=0 the arc is a zero-length point AT the declared base orientation and the visible span stays inside [base, base+sweepDir·arcAngle] ≤ arcAngle. (2) Drove the sweep against (duration − dt) instead of duration so progress hits 1.0 one frame before done — the last VISIBLE frame now lands the leading edge EXACTLY at base + sweepDir·arcAngle (no tolerance). Lifetime/done semantics unchanged (elapsed >= duration − EPS). Updated header to document both behaviors. Added tests: first-visible-frame starts AT base (trail==lead==base), full-lifetime span bound in both sweep directions, exact endpoint reach (unit + end-to-end), clockwise wake lag past the clamp. Adjusted existing sweep-rate assertions to the new (duration−dt) mapping.
summary.tradeoffs: Sweep rate is now arcAngle/(duration−dt) rad/s instead of arcAngle/duration — negligible (~1% faster) but makes the full angle visible on the last drawn frame, which is the acceptance contract. The 'sweepDirection -1' test needed a longer elapsed time (30·dt) because with the default 90° arc and 1s duration the lead only crosses wakeSpan after ~6 frames.
summary.lessons_learned: The original formula 'trail = lead − sweepDir·wakeSpan' was wrong for clockwise sweeps: it extended the wake in the WRONG direction (past the endpoint, not toward the base). For CW the wake must extend in +angle from the lead (i.e. lead + wakeSpan), clamped to base. Verified by tracing the per-frame angles before fixing.

summary.tradeoffs: render() draws a white reference box as the standalone/theater fallback (no real sprite exists for null-carrier demos), while the renderer-consumed path is the pure alpha() query — both read the same ramp so values are identical; no engine or render.js changes were made (renderer integration of alpha() is left to the consuming entity per the M6 pattern).
summary.done: Created petal-panic/js/effects/fadeOut.js (sprite-state alpha-multiplier effect, effects.md §17) and registered 'fade-out' in registry.js (one import + one registerEffect line). Added deterministic pure-unit test petal-panic/js/test/fadeOut.test.js (28 assertions, fixed dt=1/60, recording-canvas stub); verified via run-all.mjs (54/54, zero ✗) and 10× flake re-run of the new test.
summary.lessons_learned: The plan's listed verification file effectCatalog.test.js does not exist yet (M7 deliverable), so verification was done against run-all.mjs plus a dedicated per-effect test following the established per-effect test convention (attackArc/spriteFlash pattern).
summary.decisions: Sprite-state application: expose an alpha MULTIPLIER (starts at 1.0, eases toward endOpacity/startOpacity) via a pure alpha() query the renderer folds into globalAlpha, mirroring how spriteFlash exposes tint state without mutating the carrier. Total lifetime == delay + duration exactly with 1e-9 epsilon done-detection; curve vocabulary linear/easeIn(p²)/easeOut(1-(1-p)²) with unknown names falling back to linear; opacities clamped to [0,1]; endOpacity > startOpacity naturally yields a fade-in from the same ramp.

summary.failures: None after fix. All 30 scalePulse assertions pass ≥10× consecutively; full suite 55/55 ×3.
summary.decisions: Kept the impl's delay+loopCount·duration lifetime model (house convention, generalizes fadeOut's delay+duration) rather than changing it; fixed the two buggy tests to declare loopCount:1 explicitly. Chose to fix the impl for the loopCount fallback bug since the doc and test name both specify 'non-positive falls back to named default'.
summary.lessons_learned: The test harness prints 'N passed' even when assertions fail because ok() counts caught failures — trust the ✗ lines + exit code. The three failing tests encoded mutually disjoint lifetime intervals (0.4s / 0.2s / 1.5s), proving no single formula could satisfy them as written — a strong signal the tests were internally inconsistent, not just off-by-one. Math.max(1, round(x)) conflates 'clamp to minimum 1' with 'fall back to default'; use an explicit >0 guard before rounding.
summary.done: Fixed three deterministically-failing assertions in scalePulse (task 6.2). Root cause: tests 1 & 2 omitted loopCount so their instances defaulted to 3 cycles while asserting single-cycle completion; test 3 exposed an impl bug where non-positive loopCount clamped to 1 instead of falling back to the named default 3. Fixed both sides minimally: added loopCount:1 to tests 1 & 2, and corrected the impl's loopCount normalization so non-positive/absent values fall back to DEFAULT_LOOP_COUNT (3) like duration/frequency. Documented the exact lifetime formula (delay + loopCount·duration) in the file header.
summary.tradeoffs: None — changes are minimal and preserve all other passing assertions (27→30 passed).

easeOut curve (fast onset, gentle settle) chosen for both windows — documented in the file header rather than exposed as a param knob since §19 lists no curve parameter; intensity clamped to [0,2] so configs can overshoot past declared targets for exaggerated impacts but never go negative.
summary.lessons_learned: The fixed-dt accumulator sits ~1e-17 just BEFORE round-tripped boundaries (e.g. 6·(1/60) = 0.0999...), so the first sampled frame after the distort window is one full dt into recovery — continuity tests must sample at elapsed+dt, not assume the boundary frame itself; run-all.mjs prints per-file ✓/✗ only, trust exitCode + ✗ lines.
summary.done: Created petal-panic/js/effects/squashStretch.js (M6 sprite-state effect, effects.md §19): exposes non-uniform xScale()/yScale() multipliers that ease from neutral 1.0 to peak 1+intensity·(target−1) over the distort window then recover back to exactly 1.0/1.0 over the recovery window; standalone/theater render() draws a centered reference box sized by EXACTLY those queries; registered as 'squash-stretch' in registry.js (one import + one line); added deterministic pure-unit test petal-panic/js/test/squashStretch.test.js (30 assertions, fixed dt=1/60).
summary.decisions: Two-window model: lifetime == delay + duration + recoveryDuration exactly (EPS 1e-9 done-detection); peaks reached at t = delay+duration and terminal values exactly 1.0 by construction of the eased progress; defaults xScale 1.4 / yScale 0.6 encode the classic landing pose (wide-and-short), flipped for jump/stretch configs; follow scalePulse's M6 pattern (multiplier query + same-value reference draw + deferred render.js consumption note for M7).

summary.done: Created petal-panic/js/effects/auraGlow.js (Aura/Glow, effects.md §22): a world-space STATE/DRAW effect that paints one filled circle behind the carrier sprite with a canvas radial gradient (color at pulsing alpha at center → transparent at edge). Pulsing radius r(t)=radius·(1+A/2·cos(2π·pulseRate·t)) and alpha(t)=opacity·intensity·(0.5+0.5·cos(2π·pulseRate·t)), both pure functions of elapsed time (no Math.random); pulseRate 0 disables the pulse (steady aura). Carrier origin() wins over params.x/y; offset shifts the drawn center; origin captured once at fire time (fixed-position contract, no followTarget). Lifetime == duration exactly with EPS=1e-9 done-detection. Registered as 'aura-glow' in registry.js (one import + one registerEffect line, no engine change). Added deterministic pure-unit test petal-panic/js/test/auraGlow.test.js (27 assertions) with a recording-canvas stub that captures createRadialGradient/addColorStop so the gradient draw is asserted.
summary.tradeoffs: Radius pulse uses cos (starts at +A/2 above base at t=0) while alpha uses 0.5+0.5·cos (starts at full peak) — documented explicitly in the header rather than forcing both to share one waveform; keeps the documented 't=0 starts at FULL peak opacity' contract for the alpha while giving the radius a symmetric ±A/2 swing around the declared base. Color is parsed from hex/rgb() into rgba(r,g,b,a) stops because canvas gradient stops need explicit alpha per stop; unparseable colors fall back to black channels (documented).
summary.decisions: Chose a DRAW effect (paints its own geometry via createRadialGradient) rather than an M6 multiplier pattern — §22 is a glow BEHIND the sprite, not a sprite-state modifier, so it needs no renderer-side consumption hook. Fixed-origin (no followTarget) matches groundMarker's contract; a continuously-following aura would be re-fired each frame by a continuous declaration. save/restore brackets the geometry draw only (gradient object created before the bracket since it carries no canvas state). intensity clamped [0,2] mirroring squashStretch's convention (0 = invisible degenerate config, >1 = flaring overshoot).
summary.lessons_learned: The plan's listed verify command (effectCatalog.test.js) does not exist yet — it is an M7 deliverable; verified via the new per-effect unit test + run-all.mjs instead. The ok() helper increments its count even on caught failure, so trust the ✗ lines + process.exitCode, not the trailing 'N passed'. First implementation of the radius pulse used the same 0.5+0.5·cos waveform as the alpha, which made pulseRate=0 yield radius·1.25 instead of the documented constant base radius — fixed by switching the radius to a plain cos term with an explicit pulseRate>EPS guard, matching the documented 'pulseRate 0 disables the pulse' contract.
